To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
surface-imprinted magnetic fluorescent beads were synthesized via RAFT polymerization, which showed a selective binding ability toward the template molecule.

a general method for the preparation of surface-imprinted fluorescent magnetic nanoparticles via reversible chain transfer polymerization has been presented, and that the resulting composites exhibit high fluorescence intensity, good selectivity and magnetic property.

a facile method for the preparation of molecular imprinting polymers onto fluorescein coated magnetic nanoparticles has been successfully developed, and the resulting magnetic fluorescent beads exhibited homogeneous polymer film, spherical shape, high magnetic property, high fluorescence intensity, and good imprinting ability.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a novel surface imprinting method via RAFT polymerization.
a novel strategy for preparing magnetic molecularly imprinted fluorescence beads.
a facile and efficient method for the preparation of molecularly imputed fluorescent magnetic nanospheres, which may have a great potential in the field of environmental monitoring and analysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

surface molecular imprinting onto fluorescence-coated magnetic nanoparticles provides a facile three-in one system for the recognition and removal of endocrine disrupting compounds from the environment.
surface molecular imprinting is a powerful tool to produce magnetic fluorescence beads with high recognition and separation efficiency for endocrine disrupting chemicals.

the present work has successfully developed an efficient and facile approach to the synthesis of magnetic molecularly imprinted fluorescence beads for the recognition and removal of endocrine disrupting chemical 17β- estradiol.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the surface molecularly imprinting onto fluorescing magnetic nanoparticles via RAFT polymerization is a simple, efficient and green approach for the fabrication of a three-in-one system with the ability to simultaneously recognize and separate endocrine disrupting chemicals.
the as-synthesized composites are expected to be promising materials for the detection and removal of endocrine disrupting compounds from water.

the magnetic fluorescence beads can be prepared by surface molecular imprinting via reversible addition- fragmentation chain transfer polymerizations and the resulting hybrids can be used as a simple and efficient tool for the recognition and removal of endocrine disrupting pollutants.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the surface-imprinting technique can be extended to other templates of interest and the resulting materials can be further exploited for various applications.
the surface-imprinted magnetic beads can be used as a simple three-in-one system (recognition, separation and fluorescence detection) to detect endocrine disrupting chemicals.
